subject: Onboarding: Performance sync and acceptance test plan for Velotech
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@velotech.com>, Saira Khan <saira.k@velotech.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: Performance acceptance checklist + timing

Hi Daniel & Saira,

Thanks for the quick signals yesterday. To keep the onboarding momentum, attached is a short operational checklist for the performance handoff and a proposed 48-hour window for the acceptance run. Key asks:

- Confirm the production-like dataset we'll use for the run (anonymized)
- Confirm IP allowlist for our load generator (list in the YAML)
- Sign off on the latency & throughput targets we propose below

Targets we're proposing for initial acceptance:
- Median per-token latency (95th percentile L2 path): <= 120ms
- P95 tail latency per request (end-to-end): <= 450ms under nominal workload
- Sustained throughput: 120 concurrent User-agents at target QPS (equivalent to ~900 req/min)
- Error rate: <0.5% 5xx across the run

I've looped in Irene (platform lead) and Monica (CS). If those targets look off, flag them and we can adjust. Proposed acceptance window: 2028-08-18 09:00-21:00 PT (12-hour test + buffer).

Attachments: velotech-loadplan.yaml (IP allowlist + env), k6-scripts.tar.gz (load scripts).

Next step: Daniel, can you confirm the datasets and test window by COB today?

Thanks,
Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@velotech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Saira Khan <saira.k@velotech.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-17T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Performance acceptance checklist + timing

Ben,

Thanks — that looks like a good starting point. Quick confirmations from our side:

- Dataset: We'll provide a 20k-record anonymized sample that mirrors production token distributions. Delivery ETA: 2028-08-17 16:00 PT (upload to the Drive link you shared).
- IP allowlist: Confirmed, we'll open inbound from the two Redwood generator IPs in velotech staging.
- Targets: Median/tail targets look reasonable. We'd like to add one request-level SLA: 99th percentile latency <= 700ms under the sustained throughput. Is that feasible?
- Window: 2028-08-18 09:00-21:00 PT works for our SREs.

Also please include any expected warm-up traffic pattern — we prefer a gradual ramp over 20 minutes to prime caches.

We'll have Saira and our infra lead on call during the run.

Thanks,
Daniel
Senior Product Ops, Velotech

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@velotech.com>, Saira Khan <saira.k@velotech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-17T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Performance acceptance checklist + timing

Hi Daniel & Saira — thanks, and great questions. Below is the technical runbook we'll execute; I've included explicit checks, measurement points, and the acceptance criteria including your 99th percentile ask. Please review and confirm.

Runbook (summary):
- Environment: Redwood Dedicated staging pool (pinned model: rwd-llama-3-13b-q4), sequence length capped at 1024 tokens for the run.
- Test generator: k6 scripts (attached). Ramp: 0 -> 60 users over 10 minutes, then 60 -> 120 over next 10 minutes. Hold 10 hours, then ramp down over 20 minutes.
- Warmup: 30 minutes of low QPS synthetic traffic to populate KV cache and embeddings cache.
- Measurement endpoints: /v1/generate (chat), /v1/embeddings (sampling), per-request timing from client-to-client (including DNS/TLS).

Acceptance criteria (finalized):
- Median per-token latency (p50): <= 100ms (we tightened from Ben's note after running internal pre-checks).
- P95 end-to-end latency per request: <= 450ms
- P99 end-to-end latency per request: <= 700ms (Velotech request — accepted)
- Sustained throughput: 120 concurrent virtual users with error rate <0.5%
- 95% of requests should have KV cache hits for repeated prefixes (validation metric)

Data collection & artifacts we will share:
- k6 raw metrics and summary CSV (velotech-results-20280818.csv)
- Per-request traces for 1% sampled traffic (linked in Drive)
- Token-level latency breakdown (server-side logs) and per-route cost estimate

Pre-run checklist (must be done before 08/18 08:00 PT):
1) Velotech upload anonymized dataset to the shared Drive folder (Ben's link).
2) Confirm allowlist completed for Redwood load generator IPs.
3) Agree on a single assertion set for pass/fail (we recommend using the criteria above).
4) Ensure an on-call path: velotech SRE + Redwood infra lead (Monica).

If you confirm, we'll execute the run and upload artifacts within 3 hours of completion.

Attachments referenced: velotech-loadplan.yaml, k6-scripts.tar.gz

Regards,
Irene Choi
Director, Platform Engineering — Redwood Inference

From: Saira Khan <saira.k@velotech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@velotech.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-19T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Performance acceptance checklist + timing

Irene & team,

Thanks for the runbook and for tightening the median target. We executed on 2028-08-18 per the plan. High-level readout:

- Run window: 2028-08-18 09:05-21:10 PT (small delays due to VPN cert rotation)
- Sustained throughput: 120 virtual users held for 10 hours (k6 steady state)
- Error rate: 0.18% 5xx observed (within threshold)
- Median per-token latency p50: 94ms
- P95 end-to-end: 430ms
- P99 end-to-end: 655ms

Artifacts uploaded to Drive: velotech-results-20280818.csv, k6-summaries/trace-1pct/, server-side-token-latency.csv

Conclusion: We consider the run a pass against the agreed acceptance criteria. A couple of notes for the next phase:
- We saw elevated tail latency during a brief cache-eviction event (~17:40 PT) — logs and trace attached.
- We'd like to schedule a 90-minute retrospective with Redwood infra to discuss cache configuration and a plan to reduce P99 to <600ms in the next sprint.

Thanks for the smooth coordination — Monica, can you pick 3 slots next week for the retro?

Best,
Saira Khan
SRE Lead, Velotech
